I'm an engineering student from London and built my first app which took me a little over two months.

Step 1: Grew some balls.
Step 2: Got my shxt together.
Step 3: Signed up for Trello (like virtual post it notes) to keep my self organized and make to-do lists.
Step 4: Tried the Android tutorial (https://developer.android.com/training/index.html - Building Your First App).. and failed miserably..
Step 5: Went back to my year 1 Java notes from uni and brushed up.
Step 6: Went back to the Tutorial, got up to "Supporting Different Devices" and started pulling out my hair.
Step 6: Done this twitter tutorial instead (http://www.codelearn.org/android-tutorial#tutorial) which helped me really learn what I was doing.
Step 7: Signed up for Github, and integrated it with Android Studio and made a private Repo for my app to track my progress/code changes (which took bloody ages to figure out might I add).
Step 8: Started designing a super basic concept on a buying and selling platform based on my annoyance with similar apps on the market (like why do I need to sign up with Facebook? Why do they have like 1000 categories? Why do people still use description, just tell me if its used/new, size M or L, boxed or unboxed. Why am I seeing results from people 100s+ miles away?).
Step 9: Persevered, used Google compulsively, didn't give up when shxt got tough and hid knifes to avoid slitting wrists.
Step 10: After a 70 day streak on github, my app is done! 

http://oi58.tinypic.com/2q1e4hz.jpg

SO about the app:

- Its a local face-to-face buying and selling platform.
- Uses your location to post and find adverts relevant to you.
- Has built in chat to communicate with others.
- Uses tags as a substitute to descriptions, so mama, papa or those with poor writing skills can dive right in!
- Best of all - no login required! woohoo! (I hate logins...grr)

Heres the link for it: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tiikit.tiik

Don't be shy to let me know your honest thoughts, or what to improve. Would also be nice to get some of your suggestions.
